name: Anthropic /code-review
model_policy: DECLARED vs OBSERVED — they differ, and the observed one is what the numbers rest on. DECLARED (the plugin's commands/code-review.md, verbatim): 5 parallel Sonnet review agents (step 4); 'Use a Haiku agent' for eligibility, CLAUDE.md path discovery, PR summary, per-issue confidence scoring and the re-check (steps 1/2/3/5/7); only the orchestrator on the session model. OBSERVED from every cell's meter.json modelUsage (2026-08-19): NO HAIKU IN ANY CELL. The scoreable cells run Sonnet 60-67% of cost with the Opus 5 orchestrator taking the rest; two cells ran Opus 5 only, with no Sonnet lane dispatched at all. The plugin pins models in PROSE ('use a Haiku agent'), not by an enforced model parameter, so the pin is a request the orchestrator did not honour. Consequence: this arm is dearer and more capable than its declared policy implies, and the earlier claim that 'its reviewers sit at a DIFFERENT cutoff than the rest of the roster' does not hold for the observed models — Sonnet 5 and Opus 5 are the same generation as BENCH_MODEL. Re-verify with modelUsage rather than trusting this field: the plugin ships unversioned ('Version: unknown') and was reinstalled from marketplace HEAD on 2026-08-18.
invocation: Use the Skill tool to run `code-review:code-review` — the plugin-qualified command from code-review@claude-plugins-official. It is NOT `decaf-quality:code-review`: a different tool ships a skill of the same bare name, so never invoke a bare `/code-review`, and abort rather than substituting anything else if the qualified skill does not resolve. Review pull request #{PR} of the GitHub repository {REPO}. Do NOT pass --comment and do NOT post anything to GitHub — output the review to the terminal only. Fetch the PR with gh. Print every finding you would post, with file:line references.
observed_models_note: The four `2__anthropic-code-review__*` cells ran claude-opus-4-8 at 100% of cost. That is an older BENCH_MODEL from an earlier era of the corpus, NOT the tool pinning a model — and those four cells are DO NOT SCORE (isolation MISSING) regardless. No scoreable cell used opus-4-8.

invocation: Use the Skill tool to run /decaf-quality-dev:code-review with arguments: bugs reach=norm --report
baseline_note: The TREATMENT arm of dcc-tmz2. Probed first (r0, never scored): the override is not a no-op — the narrow report omits Pre-existing Issues and Minor Findings and says so, the norm report carries both and states 'reach=norm overriding the preset default of narrow'. Result: higher defect-pool hit rate per cell (0.458 vs narrow 0.375) and the demotion gap falls from 0.72 to 0.41, at ~12% more cost and 8% noise. PROVISIONAL — two subjects.
